Subject: PO 4321 attached — invoicing / tax split clarifications

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Please find attached our PO (Acme_PO_4321.pdf). A couple of quick items we need clarified before procurement signs: 1) We have two legal entities — Acme Inc. (US) and Acme UK Ltd — and need some charges billed to the UK side for VAT purposes. Can Redwood split invoices by entity or by line item? 2) Our standard net terms are Net 30 but finance has flexibility to Net 45 if Redwood needs. 3) Do you require a tax residency certificate or VAT registration to avoid withholding or to determine VAT handling?

Can you confirm your suggested flow and any documentation you need from us?

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Ellis
Senior Sourcing Manager, Acme Corp

Subject: Re: PO 4321 attached — invoicing / tax split clarifications

Hi Tom — thanks for sending the PO. Looping in Ben (Billing/Ops) and Lauren (Commercial/Procurement) to align on the mechanics.

Short answers up front:
- We can invoice multiple legal entities but need the following: legal entity name, VAT/Tax ID, billing address for each entity, and which line items map to which entity.
- We can support split-line invoicing (one PDF with separate entity sections) or separate invoices per entity — both are operationally possible; Ben will advise on recommended approach.
- For VAT/withholding, a VAT certificate (or equivalent) helps determine reverse charge eligibility; if Acme provides the UK VAT registration we can zero-rate certain pass-through items where applicable.
- Net terms: we typically bill Net 30; Net 45 is possible for enterprise orders but will need commercial approval.

I've attached a redline starter for the order form with a pricing staircase and two suggested invoice flows (see proposed-order-form_redlines_v1.docx). Action items:
1) Tom — please confirm which entity should receive the recurring usage invoices vs the activation/invoice milestone.
2) Tom — if billing to the UK entity, please send the VAT registration / tax certificate.
3) Ben — recommend whether to do split-line vs separate invoices and any downstream GL impact.
4) Lauren — confirm PO acceptance steps if we change net terms to Net 45.

Best,

Marissa Cole

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: PO 4321 attached — invoicing / tax split clarifications

Marissa / Lauren — quick ops note on feasibility.

We have two practical options:
A) Single invoice PDF with clear per-entity sections: one invoice number, but lines labeled for Entity A (Acme Inc) and Entity B (Acme UK Ltd). This keeps AR workflow simple but requires Acme to accept cross-entity grouping on one invoice.
B) Separate invoices per entity: our system issues distinct invoice numbers per legal entity and posts to separate GL accounts. Cleaner for Acme accounting; slightly more overhead on our side for reconciliation.

Recommendation: go with (B) separate invoices per legal entity given VAT/residency differences — it's less ambiguous for VAT reclaim and local audits. We can still aggregate a single remit email to Billing Ops.

Billing cadence suggestion tied to order form:
- Milestone 1: Activation fee — invoice to entity designated for activation (one-off).
- Milestone 2: Monthly usage invoices for the entity that owns the contract services.
- For minimum commit / staircase pricing: we can issue a pro-rated invoice for the first partial month and follow normal monthly cycles thereafter.

Attachment: billing-logic-diagram.png (image/png, 18KB) — shows mapping of line items to GL buckets.

I also need Acme's VAT number(s) and confirmation of which legal entity signs the order form. If they want Net 45, we need a credit approval reference and the effective date for Net 45 to put in the order form.

-ben
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: PO 4321 attached — invoicing / tax split clarifications

Tom / Procurement team —

Thanks for the PO and the clarifying notes. We can move forward on the following basis, pending the documents below:
1) Invoicing: Redwood will issue separate invoices per legal entity (Acme Inc. and Acme UK Ltd). Please indicate on the PO which line items should be billed to which entity.
2) Tax documentation: please send VAT registration for Acme UK Ltd (or equivalent). This will determine whether VAT is applied or reverse-charge applies.
3) Net terms: Redwood accepts Net 45 for this order provided the credit note is included in the order form and the effective Net 45 start date is the date of first invoice. Please confirm acceptance on your side.

Next steps for procurement: once we receive the VAT certificate + confirmation of entity mapping on the PO, we will: (a) update the order form redlines to reflect billing entities and Net 45, (b) produce the final order form and send for signature (DocuSign link), and (c) issue the activation invoice on go-live.

Kimberly — copying you for any legal flags (withholding clause or other tax representation language to add).
